sentences.en: When it was time to go,
sentences.zh: 到了该离开的时候，

sentences.en: Nelson went up alone to the bedroom where little Horatia lay fast asleep.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊独自一人上楼来到小霍拉蒂娅熟睡的卧室。

sentences.en: For a while he knelt in silent prayer by her bedside.
sentences.zh: 他在床边默默祈祷了一会儿。

sentences.en: Then, very gently, he kissed her on the forehead and went downstairs.
sentences.zh: 然后，他非常轻柔地吻了吻她的额头，然后下楼去了。

sentences.en: His boxes had been loaded aboard the coach.
sentences.zh: 他的箱子已经装上了马车。

sentences.en: Emma was crying harder than ever now.
sentences.zh: 埃玛现在哭得比以往任何时候都厉害。

sentences.en: Again, Nelson knelt on the ground in prayer and asked God to bless her.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊再次跪在地上祈祷，祈求上帝保佑她。

sentences.en: For the last time, he clasped her to his cheSt.
sentences.zh: 最后一次，他将她紧紧搂在胸前。

sentences.en: Brave Emma.
sentences.zh: 勇敢的埃玛。

sentences.en: Heroic Emma.
sentences.zh: 英雄般的埃玛。

sentences.en: You encourage me to go forth.
sentences.zh: 你鼓励我继续前行。

sentences.en: He said gently.
sentences.zh: 他温柔地说。

sentences.en: If there were more Emmas, there would be more Nelsons.
sentences.zh: 如果能有更多的埃玛，就会有更多的纳尔逊。

sentences.en: Then, he climbed up into the coach and raised his left hand and he was gone.
sentences.zh: 然后，他登上马车，举起左手，便离去了。

sentences.en: Afterwards, Nelson wrote in his journal.
sentences.zh: 此后，纳尔逊在日记中写道。

sentences.en: Friday night.
sentences.zh: 星期五晚上。

sentences.en: At half past ten drove from dear, dear Merton, where I left all which I hold dear in this world, to go to serve my king and country.
sentences.zh: 十点半，我从亲爱的、亲爱的默顿出发，那里留下了我在这个世界上所珍视的一切，去为我的国王和国家效劳。

sentences.en: May the great God whom I adore enable me to fill the expectations of my country.
sentences.zh: 愿我所崇拜的伟大的上帝使我能够不负国家的期望。

sentences.en: And if it is his good pleasure that I should return, my thanks will never cease being offered up to the throne of his mercy.
sentences.zh: 如果蒙他美恩准我归来，我对他的慈悲宝座的感恩将永无止境。

sentences.en: If it is his good providence to cut short my days upon earth,
sentences.zh: 如果承蒙他美意缩短我在世间的寿数，

sentences.en: I bow with the greatest submission, relying that he will protect those so dear to me that I leave behind.
sentences.zh: 我将怀着无比顺从的心情俯首听命，坚信他会保护我留下的这些至爱之人。

sentences.en: His will be done.
sentences.zh: 愿主旨意得成。

sentences.en: Amen.
sentences.zh: 阿门。

sentences.en: Amen.
sentences.zh: 阿门。

sentences.en: Amen.
sentences.zh: 阿门。

sentences.en: An unbelievably moving scene.
sentences.zh: 令人难以置信的感人场景。

sentences.en: I mean, how I got through that without choking up, I do not know.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我不知道我是怎么在没有哽咽的情况下挺过去的。

sentences.en: It's the last farewell of Horatio Nelson to his beloved Emma, Lady Hamilton, and their daughter Horatia on the evening of the 13th of September, 1805.
sentences.zh: 这是霍雷肖·纳尔逊在 1805 年 9 月 13 日的傍晚，向他深爱的埃玛、汉密尔顿爵士夫人以及他们的女儿霍拉蒂娅做出的最后告别。

sentences.en: Dominic, it has been described many times, but I doubt it has ever been described in more powerful and emotional terms than in that passage of prose,
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，这一幕已经被描述过很多次了，但我怀疑是否曾有人用比这段散文更具力量和情感的词汇来描述过它，

sentences.en: which comes from Adventures in Time, Nelson, Hero of the Seas.
sentences.zh: 这段文字出自《时间的冒险：纳尔逊，海上英雄》。

sentences.en: And you don't need me to tell you that you wrote it.
sentences.zh: 不用我说你也知道这是你写的。

sentences.en: And can I just compliment you on giving proper credence to Emma's report of his parting words to her?
sentences.zh: 我能赞美你一下吗？你对埃玛转述的他对她的临别赠言给予了应有的信任，

sentences.en: If there were more Emma's, there would be more Nelsons because there are some black-hearted biographers who have doubted that he ever said that.
sentences.zh: “如果能有更多的埃玛，就会有更多的纳尔逊”，因为有些心地阴暗的传记作家曾怀疑他是否说过这话。

sentences.en: It's the kind of melodramatic thing that Nelson would say there, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这正是纳尔逊那种会说出的富有戏剧色彩的话，对吧？

sentences.en: I agree.
sentences.zh: 我同意。

sentences.en: I think, I absolutely think he said it.
sentences.zh: 我想，我绝对认为他说过。

sentences.en: The thing is, I'm not a massive Lady Hamilton fan, as you know, but it strikes me as absolutely plausible that Nelson turned his departure,
sentences.zh: 问题是，如你所知，我并不是汉密尔顿爵士夫人的超级粉丝，但我认为纳尔逊把他的离别，

sentences.en: that both of them actually turned his departure into this enormously sort of melodramatic theatrical spectacle.
sentences.zh: 或者说他们俩实际上把他的离别变成了一种非常具有戏剧色彩的宏大奇观，这绝对是合情合理的。

sentences.en: And actually, that's what this week's episodes are going to be, a massively melodramatic theatrical spectacle.
sentences.zh: 事实上，本周的剧集正是要讲述这样一个充满戏剧张力的宏大奇观。

sentences.en: Because it is, I think, the most dramatic, the most exciting, the most emotionally charged story in naval history,
sentences.zh: 因为我认为，这是海军史上、可以说也是整个英国历史上最具戏剧性、最激动人心、最饱含情感的故事，这就是纳尔逊驶向特拉法加命运之日的最后航程。

sentences.en: arguably in all British history, Nelson's last voyage to the day of destiny at Trafalgar.
sentences.zh: 从我们已经讲过一次这一点就能衡量出它的分量。

sentences.en: And the measure of that is that we've already done it once.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，这真的是我们唯一在重新讲述的伟大故事。

sentences.en: So this is, I think, is really the only great story that we're retelling.
sentences.zh: 但这一次我们讲述它的重点是纳尔逊本人，对吧？

sentences.en: But this time we're telling it with a focus on Nelson himself, aren't we?
sentences.zh: 是的，因为上次我们做关于特拉法加的三集节目时，

sentences.en: Yeah, because last time when we did three episodes about Trafalgar,
sentences.zh: 我们是以某种方式来看待它的，我们运用了我们在海军、军事历史、缆绳、火炮、战列舰方面的所有知识。

sentences.en: we looked at it in a sort of, we brought all our knowledge of naval, military history, rope, guns, ships of the line.
sentences.zh: 但现在我们带来了我们的心理洞察，从纳尔逊自己的视角来讨论它，对吧？

sentences.en: But now we're bringing our psychological insight to discuss it from Nelson's own perspective, aren't we?
sentences.zh: 至少这是个借口。

sentences.en: At least that's the excuse.
sentences.zh: 所以这位伟人将永远处于前景之中。

sentences.en: So the great man will always be in the foreground.
sentences.zh: 也许对于那些从一开始就与我们同行这段航程的人来说，我们可以做一个小小的回顾。

sentences.en: And maybe for those people who've been on this voyage with us from the beginning, we can just do a little recap.
sentences.zh: 所以上次，汤姆，我们的时间停在了 1805 年 7 月。

sentences.en: So last time, Tom, we ended July 1805.
sentences.zh: 用《怒海争锋》中罗素·克劳的话说，英格兰正受到入侵的威胁。

sentences.en: And to quote Russell Crowe in Master and Commander, England is under threat of invasion.
sentences.zh: 所以在两年之后……

sentences.en: So after two years...
sentences.zh: 这不是一件好笑的事。

sentences.en: It's not a laughing matter.
sentences.zh: 不，事实上不是。

sentences.en: No, it's not, actually.
sentences.zh: 我不该笑的。

sentences.en: I shouldn't be laughing.
sentences.zh: 我笑是为了阻止自己因爱国主义而泣不成声。

sentences.en: I'm laughing to stop myself sobbing with patriarchy.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 所以在海上度过了两年之后，纳尔逊一直在追击法国和西班牙的联合舰队，

sentences.en: So after two years at sea, Nelson has pursued the combined fleet of France and Spain
sentences.zh: 这支舰队由皮埃尔-夏尔·维尔纳夫和费德里科·格拉维纳率领，一路追到了加勒比海，又一路追了回来。

sentences.en: under Pierre-Charles Villeneuve and Federico Gravina, all the way to the Caribbean and all the way back.
sentences.zh: 而维尔纳夫躲进了西班牙北部港口费罗尔。

sentences.en: And Villeneuve has holed up in the northern Spanish port of Ferrol.
sentences.zh: 所以威胁暂时消退了。

sentences.en: So the threat has faded for the time being.
sentences.zh: 它被遏制住了，但并没有完全消失。

sentences.en: It's been bottled up, but it hasn't completely disappeared.
sentences.zh: 这让纳尔逊在经历了多年海上的封锁任务后，终于有机会回家去看看他深爱的埃玛。

sentences.en: And that gives Nelson the chance, after all these years at sea, on his blockading mission, to go home at last to see his beloved Emma.
sentences.zh: 他于 8 月 19 日星期一在朴次茅斯登陆。

sentences.en: And he lands in Portsmouth on Monday, the 19th of AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 当他到达那里时，重现了他登陆英国的一个特色场景，那就是人们决心解开他马车上的马匹，

sentences.en: And when he gets there, there's a reprise of what's been a feature of his landing in England, which is the determination of people to unhitch the horses from his carriage
sentences.zh: 亲自抬他、拉他前进，同时伴随着轻骑兵的呼喊。

sentences.en: and to carry him, to pull him himself, while doing hussars.
sentences.zh: 这衡量出纳尔逊急于回到埃玛身边的心情是多么迫切。

sentences.en: And it's the measure of how desperate Nelson is to get back to Emma.
sentences.zh: 但这一次，当他们试图解下马轭时，他坚决不许，因为他急着脱身。

sentences.en: But this time, when they try and unyoke the horses, he won't let them, because he's desperate to get off.
sentences.zh: 他可不吃这一套。

sentences.en: And he's not having any of this business.
sentences.zh: 你在我们开始录制之前告诉我，你希望澳大利亚人在我们抵达澳大利亚进行历史之旅时也为我们这样做。

sentences.en: You were telling me before we started recording, that you were hoping that Australians would do this for us when we arrived in Australia for our History Tour.
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: That's right, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我们很乐意体验一下轻骑兵式的欢呼。

sentences.en: We'd love some hazarring.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Definitely.
sentences.zh: 还有人们拉着我们、拉着马车。

sentences.en: And people pulling us, pulling the carriage.
sentences.zh: 我认为这非常重要。

sentences.en: I think that's very important.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，他出发了。

sentences.en: Anyway, so he sets off.
sentences.zh: 他急忙赶往默顿。

sentences.en: He rushes to Merton.
sentences.zh: 第二天清晨，他的马车驶入了默顿庄园新建的马车道。

sentences.en: And early the next day, his coach turns into the new carriageway that has been built at Merton Place.
sentences.zh: 埃玛已经焦虑地等了他两年。

sentences.en: Now, Emma has been waiting anxiously for him for two years.
sentences.zh: 她一直在滨海绍森德进行海水浴。

sentences.en: She's been sea bathing in Southend-on-Sea.
sentences.zh: 海水浴在英国变得非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: Which has become massively popular in England.
sentences.zh: 布赖顿是人们去进行海水浴的著名地方。

sentences.en: So Brighton is the famous place where people go to do it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，埃玛在意大利时就已经迷上了洗浴，因为她的丈夫威廉·汉密尔顿爵士从英国给她买了一台洗澡车，

sentences.en: And Emma had actually become a fan of bathing in Italy, because Sir William Hamilton, her husband, had brought her a bathing machine from England
sentences.zh: 这样她就可以保护自己的肤色免受意大利阳光的伤害。

sentences.en: so that she could protect her complexion from the Italian sun.
sentences.zh: 所以她对洗浴非常熟悉。

sentences.en: So she's very au fait with bathing.
sentences.zh: 这车是怎么防晒的？

sentences.en: How does the machine protect you from the sun?
sentences.zh: 我想你是把它开出去，对吧？

sentences.en: I think you drive it out, don't you?
sentences.zh: 然后你把脚伸出去防晒。

sentences.en: And so you put your feet out and protect you.
sentences.zh: 但你基本上是被某种形式的屋顶遮盖着的。

sentences.en: But you're basically covered by some form of roof.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我在这里正遭到关于洗澡车的问题的伏击。

sentences.en: I'm being ambushed here by questions about bathing machines.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 如果你没有准备好探讨这个细节，你就不该把它写进去。

sentences.en: You shouldn't have put that detail in if you weren't prepared to explore it.
sentences.zh: 对，我知道，我知道。

sentences.en: Yeah, I know, I know.
sentences.zh: 总之，她赶回家。

sentences.en: Well, anyway, she rushes home.
sentences.zh: 她兴奋得无以复加。

sentences.en: She's incredibly excited.
sentences.zh: 在听到他归来的消息后，她安排人把现在已经四岁的霍拉蒂娅从吉布森太太（她的监护人）那里接了过来。

sentences.en: And she has arranged, I'm hearing the news of his return, to have Horatia, who is now four, brought from Mrs. Gibson, who is her kind of guardian.
sentences.zh: 所以纳尔逊当他到达默顿时，看到霍拉蒂娅格外高兴。

sentences.en: So Nelson, when he arrives at Merton, he is absolutely overjoyed to see Horatia in particular.
sentences.zh: 他还没有正式承认她是自己的骨肉，对吧？

sentences.en: Who he hasn't officially acknowledged as his own, has he?
sentences.zh: 没有，但他真的很溺爱她。

sentences.en: No, but he really dotes on her.
sentences.zh: 他安排她去上主日学校。

sentences.en: He makes arrangements for her to go to Sunday school.
sentences.zh: 他当然是一位牧师的儿子，所以他对此非常认真。

sentences.en: He is, of course, the son of a vicar, so he takes that very seriously.
sentences.zh: 我想大家都有这样一种期望，即他希望霍拉蒂娅能与他们永久生活在一起，并且从这时起就住在默顿。

sentences.en: I think there's an expectation, don't you, that he would like Horatia to live with them permanently, and Merton from this point onwards.
sentences.zh: 他也对这所房子赞不绝口。

sentences.en: And he's also thrilled with the house.
sentences.zh: 我提到了新的马车道。

sentences.en: I mentioned the new carriageway.
sentences.zh: 埃玛在过去的两年里对房子做了很多工作。

sentences.en: Emma has done a lot of work in the last two years on the house.
sentences.zh: 某种宏大的设计已经完成，她拥有了一个新厨房。

sentences.en: Sort of grand designs have been in, and she has got a new kitchen.
sentences.zh: 有一个新图书馆，还有大量他和埃玛自己的新画像。

sentences.en: There's a new library, loads of new pictures of Nelson and herself.
sentences.zh: 这才是关键，关键所在。

sentences.en: That's the key, the key thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上这里原本有两栋房子，她把它们缝合在了一起，并买下了周围的大片产业，

sentences.en: I mean, basically, there were kind of two houses, and she's knitted them together, and she's bought up lots of estates around it,
sentences.zh: 所以这里比纳尔逊离开时要气派得多。

sentences.en: so that it's a much more prepossessing place than when Nelson had left.
sentences.zh: 她也把自己想象成一个园林设计师，因为我想纳尔逊曾说过她简直是个常规的布朗能力（造园大师），或者是类似的人物。

sentences.en: And she fancied herself as a garden designer as well, because Nelson, I think, said she was a regular capability brown, or something of that ilk.
sentences.zh: 天哪，她的才华真是无止境。

sentences.en: God, there's no end to her talents.
sentences.zh: 是的，太惊人了。

sentences.en: Yeah, amazing.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，纳尔逊在默顿呆的时间并没有他希望的那么长，因为他的主要事务在伦敦。

sentences.en: But actually, Nelson doesn't spend as much time at Merton as he would like, because his main business is in London.
sentences.zh: 就在到达默顿的第二天，他便前往伦敦会见政府和海军部的各种大人物。

sentences.en: The very next day, after arriving in Merton, he goes into London to meet various kind of bigwigs from the government and the admiralty.
sentences.zh: 其中最主要的是威廉·皮特，即小皮特（他是首相），以及新的战争大臣卡尔斯雷勋爵。

sentences.en: Chief among them, William Pitt, Pitt the Younger, who is prime minister, and the new secretary of state for war, who is Lord Castlereagh.
sentences.zh: 当他到达那里时，纳尔逊非常担心自己会遭到指责，人们会因为他没能抓住维尔纳夫而让他吃尽苦头，

sentences.en: And when he gets there, Nelson is quite anxious that he will be, that people will give him a lot of grief for failing to catch a field nerve,
sentences.zh: 因为那当然是他的野心，去追赶联合舰队并将其消灭。

sentences.en: because that, of course, was his ambition, to catch up with the combined fleet and to destroy it.
sentences.zh: 所以他有点担心人们会说，天哪，你让我们失望了。

sentences.en: So he's a little bit anxious, people will say, gosh, you've let us down.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，当他到达伦敦时，他发现报纸正欢呼他是拯救加勒比海的英雄，

sentences.en: But actually, when he gets there to London, he finds that the newspapers are hailing him as the man who has saved the Caribbean
sentences.zh: 拯救了英国的西印度群岛殖民地，也就是对英国经济繁荣至关重要的糖岛。

sentences.en: for Britain, the West Indian colony, basically the Sugar Islands, which are so important to Britain's economic prosperity.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我也认为他们是在赞赏他在如此严酷的环境下保持舰队凝聚力并确保维尔纳夫一事无成所取得的成就规模。

sentences.en: Well, I mean, also, I think they're recognising the scale of his accomplishment in keeping his fleet together under such gruelling circumstances
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这完全正确。

sentences.en: and ensuring that Villeneuve can't do anything.
sentences.zh: 我认为他现在，在这一点上——我们在之前的剧集里谈到过类似他在乡间巡游之类的事情——

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's completely right.
sentences.zh: 嗯，对的。

sentences.en: I think he is now, at this point, we've talked in previous episodes about things like when he went on a kind of progress around the countryside
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: and people were hailing him and stuff.
sentences.zh: 人们欢呼雀跃，甚至还有各种举动。

sentences.en: He is a genuine celebrity.
sentences.zh: 他是个真正的名流。

sentences.en: He is the supreme patriotic hero.
sentences.zh: 他是至高无上的民族英雄。

sentences.en: So an American tourist afterwards described seeing him in the Strand.
sentences.zh: 因此，一位美国游客事后描述了他在河岸街（The Strand）看到他的情景。

sentences.en: His son burnt, of course, because he's been at sea all this time.
sentences.zh: 他的儿子自然晒黑了，因为他一直在海上待了这么久。

sentences.en: He walks with the sailor's gait, so he has this amusing sort of rolling walk.
sentences.zh: 他走起路来带有水手的步态，所以有一种十分有趣的摇摆步态。

sentences.en: And this American said, when he enters a shop, the door is thronged till he comes out, when the air rings with huzzas and the dark cloud of the populace again moves on
sentences.zh: 这位美国人说，当他走进一家店铺时，门外挤满了人，直到他出来时，空气中回荡着欢呼声，黑压压的民众又继续向前移动

sentences.en: and hangs upon his skirts.
sentences.zh: 并簇拥在他身边。

sentences.en: He's a great favourite with all descriptions of people.
sentences.zh: 他深受各阶层人士的喜爱。

sentences.en: It's going to be like us in Sydney.
sentences.zh: 这就像我们在悉尼的遭遇一样。

sentences.en: It is, very similar scenes, actually.
sentences.zh: 确实是的，情景非常相似。

sentences.en: And his mate, Lord Minto, whom we've encountered previously being extremely disparaging about the menage at Merton and the interior decoration.
sentences.zh: 还有他的伙伴明托勋爵（Lord Minto），我们以前曾遇到过他对默顿（Merton）的家政和室内装饰极其不屑。

sentences.en: Lord Minto came across him in Piccadilly and found him mobbed by a crowd and actually went into the crowd to kind of get him out and said afterwards,
sentences.zh: 明托勋爵在皮卡迪利大街（Piccadilly）偶遇了他，发现他被人群包围，于是竟然挤进人群把他拉了出来，事后他说：

sentences.en: it was affecting to see the wonder and admiration and love and respect of the whole world the moment he is seen.
sentences.zh: 只要一看到他，就能感受到全世界对他的惊叹、钦佩、爱戴和敬意，那场景令人动容。

sentences.en: It's beyond anything represented in a play or a poem.
sentences.zh: 这超越了戏剧或诗歌中所表现的一切。

sentences.en: And I think also for the Admiralty, they are also affected by this, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 我想对于海军部来说，他们也深受触动，不是吗？

sentences.en: The sense that he is something more now than just an admiral or an officer to be slotted into a chain of command, that his fame and his charisma have transcended that,
sentences.zh: 那种感觉是，他现在不仅仅是一个可以被安插在指挥链中的海军上将或军官，他的名望和个人魅力已经超越了这一点，

sentences.en: that he is the person inevitably that they're going to turn to when and if the great moment of crisis comes.
sentences.zh: 当重大危机来临时，他必然是他们首要求助的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's become, from being a slightly difficult asset, which he was a couple of years ago, he's now more than that, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 是的，从几年前一个稍微有点棘手的资产，他现在变得更重要了，对吧？

sentences.en: He's the embodiment of the naval spirit itself.
sentences.zh: 他就是海军精神本身的化身。

sentences.en: Yeah, he's an icon.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是个偶像。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I think to make sense of this, you have to see Nelson as part of a sort of a dichotomy.
sentences.zh: 我认为要理解这一点，你必须将纳尔逊视为一种对立统一体的一部分。

sentences.en: You've got Nelson on one side and you have Napoleon on the other.
sentences.zh: 一边是纳尔逊，另一边是拿破仑。

sentences.en: Because just as people are swooning before Nelson, hatred of Napoleon Bonaparte has now reached an absolute peak in Britain.
sentences.zh: 因为就在人们对纳尔逊顶礼膜拜的同时，英国上下对拿破仑·波拿巴的憎恨也达到了绝对顶点。

sentences.en: So the newspapers paint him, which had actually not been entirely unadmiring in the 1790s, now paint him as this sort of Corsican dwarf, as I quote,
sentences.zh: 因此，报纸将他描绘成这样一种科西嘉侏儒——我在引用原话，尽管在18世纪90年代时报纸并非完全不赞赏他——

sentences.en: a plunderer and murderer with a malignant spirit, a depraved imagination, and a heart black with crimes of the deepest dye.
sentences.zh: 一个怀有恶毒精神、堕落想象力以及满腔最深重罪恶黑心的掠夺者和杀人犯。

sentences.en: Our prosperity and glory, our opposition to his schemes of universal conquest, rankle in his mind and prey upon his heart,
sentences.zh: 我们的繁荣与荣耀、我们对他的全面征服计划的抵制，在他心中如芒在背，噬咬着他的心，

sentences.en: exciting that deadly enmity which will drown our island with blood.
sentences.zh: 激起了那种将用鲜血淹没我们岛屿的致命敌意。

sentences.en: So Napoleon as the bogeyman is now at his absolute height.
sentences.zh: 因此，拿破仑作为恶魔的形象现在达到了最顶峰。

sentences.en: But I mean, it's kind of interesting because obviously there are people who still admire Napoleon, and this will be the case right the way throughout the Napoleonic Wars.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，这挺有意思的，因为显然还是有人崇拜拿破仑，而且在整个拿破仑战争期间一直如此。

sentences.en: So Byron is a kind of famous example.
sentences.zh: 拜伦就是一个著名的例子。

sentences.en: But even Byron admires Nelson.
sentences.zh: 但甚至连拜伦也崇拜纳尔逊。

sentences.en: I think even the people at Holland House, the supporters of Fox and all these people, the Whigs, even they sense that in Nelson they have someone who is
sentences.zh: 我认为甚至连荷兰大宅（Holland House）的人、福克斯（Fox）的支持者以及所有这些辉格党人，他们也感觉纳尔逊拥有

sentences.en: a kind of transcendently charismatic figure.
sentences.zh: 一种超越常人的领袖魅力。

sentences.en: And I think for the mass of the public, you know, the great sweep of European history is reduced in their minds, is simplified in their minds into a clash between these two men.
sentences.zh: 我认为对于广大公众而言，你知道，宏大的欧洲历史进程在他们心中被简化、被缩小为了这两个人之间的冲突。

sentences.en: And a lot of this is because London is now in the grip of a full-blown invasion panic.
sentences.zh: 这很大程度上是因为伦敦现在正陷入全面入侵恐慌的泥潭。

sentences.en: So there are multiple invasion panics during the French Revolution and Napoleonic Wars.
sentences.zh: 所以在法国大革命和拿破仑战争期间，曾有过多次入侵恐慌。

sentences.en: This one has been building since the war resumed in 1803.
sentences.zh: 这一次自1803年战争恢复以来一直在酝酿。

sentences.en: It's fuelled by all these kind of Gilray cartoons and newspaper articles and so on.
sentences.zh: 它是由所有这些吉尔雷（Gilray）讽刺漫画、报纸文章等等推波助澜的。

sentences.en: And, you know, you would see everywhere in London, if you walk around, pictures of all the French schemes, sort of massive paddle boats
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果你在伦敦四处走走，到处都能看到法国各种计划的图片，比如巨大的明轮船

sentences.en: and fleets of balloons, a channel tunnel, all of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 和气球舰队、英吉利海峡隧道，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Yes, and I think that that's the kind of subliminal memory that carried right the way up to the building of the actual channel tunnel that exists now.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为这是一种潜意识中的记忆，一直延续到了现在实际存在的英吉利海峡隧道的建设。

sentences.en: People were kind of nervous about it.
sentences.zh: 人们对此感到有些紧张。

sentences.en: The French will attack us.
sentences.zh: 法国人会攻击我们。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: Yeah, they were.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们确实如此。

sentences.en: Completely they were.
sentences.zh: 完全是这样。

sentences.en: And it's easy for us to laugh at it and say, oh, this is overblown because we know the invasion didn't happen.
sentences.zh: 我们很容易对此付之一笑，说这言过其实，因为我们知道入侵并没有发生。

sentences.en: But there were very good reasons for people to be frightened.
sentences.zh: 但当时人们感到害怕是非常有充分理由的。

sentences.en: I mean, just to get into the invasion panic, you know, the mood that Nelson encounters when he returns in 1805.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，单就入侵恐慌而言，也就是纳尔逊1805年归来时所遇到的那种情绪。

sentences.en: If the French ever got across the channel, they would be pretty much unstoppable.
sentences.zh: 如果法国人真的渡过了海峡，他们几乎是势不可挡的。

sentences.en: Britain has only a tiny army.
sentences.zh: 英国只有一支微不足道的军队。

sentences.en: What army it had, what professional army it had, had been devastated by a failed invasion of Haiti in the 1790s and has never really been rebuilt.
sentences.zh: 它所拥有的那点军队，那支职业军队，在18世纪90年代对海地的一次失败入侵中就已经被摧毁了，而且从未真正重建过。

sentences.en: Napoleon's army, by contrast, the most formidable machine in Europe.
sentences.zh: 相比之下，拿破仑的军队是欧洲最强大的战争机器。

sentences.en: They've destroyed every enemy in their path.
sentences.zh: 他们摧毁了途中的每一个敌人。

sentences.en: They've left a trail of blood behind them, plundering and sacking all these towns and villages in Italy and so on.
sentences.zh: 他们在身后留下一条血路，在意大利等地到处掠夺和洗劫城镇村庄。

sentences.en: And it's understandable that people think if the French ever did get across the channel, you know, the consequences will be nightmarish for Britain.
sentences.zh: 人们认为如果法国人真的渡过了海峡，后果对英国来说将是噩梦般的，这是完全可以理解的。

sentences.en: But also, they only need control of the channel for a day to land their forces.
sentences.zh: 而且，他们只需要控制海峡一天就能登陆部队。

sentences.en: And then essentially, Britain would be knocked out of the war.
sentences.zh: 到那时，基本上英国就会被击出局，退出战争。

sentences.en: So there was a marshal of Napoleon, André Masséna, who said, we're never going to conquer Britain.
sentences.zh: 所以拿破仑的一位元帅安德烈·马塞纳（André Masséna）曾说，我们永远不会征服英国。

sentences.en: No one even dreamt of it.
sentences.zh: 没有人甚至梦想过这一点。

sentences.en: It was just a question of ruining it, of leaving it in a condition that no one would ever have wanted to possess it.
sentences.zh: 这只是一个毁掉它的问题，把它变成一个谁也不会想要去占有的境地。

sentences.en: And essentially, that would mean destroying the dockyards.
sentences.zh: 从根本上说，这意味着摧毁造船厂。

sentences.en: So Portsmouth.
sentences.zh: 也就是朴茨茅斯（Portsmouth）。

sentences.en: Or Chatham, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然还有查塔姆（Chatham）。

sentences.en: And Chatham would have been right in the pathway.
sentences.zh: 而查塔姆正好在必经之路上。

sentences.en: A place so close to your heart.
sentences.zh: 一个离你内心如此之近的地方。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So I think it's not entirely unjustified.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为并非完全没有道理。

sentences.en: I mean, the stakes are high.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，赌注很高。

sentences.en: If the Royal Navy loses control of the seas, Britain is sunk.
sentences.zh: 如果皇家海军失去对海洋的控制，英国就完蛋了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Nice marine metaphor there, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这里有个漂亮的海洋隐喻，汤姆。

sentences.en: Well done.
sentences.zh: 干得好。

sentences.en: That's what I'm all about.
sentences.zh: 我就是搞这个的。

sentences.en: So by August 1805, all of this has reached a climax.
sentences.zh: 因此，到1805年8月，所有这一切都达到了高潮。

sentences.en: Napoleon assembles his invasion force.
sentences.zh: 拿破仑集结了他的入侵部队。

sentences.en: It's French, Dutch and Bavarian armies.
sentences.zh: 这是法国、荷兰和巴伐利亚的军队。

sentences.en: They're camped along the coast of the Channel, all the way from Boulogne, eastwards to Antwerp, including the French cavalry and the Imperial Guard.
sentences.zh: 他们驻扎在海峡海岸，从西边的滨海布洛涅（Boulogne）一直延伸到东边的安特卫普，其中包括法国骑兵和帝国卫队。

sentences.en: So the very kind of cream of the Napoleonic war machine.
sentences.zh: 可以说是拿破仑战争机器的绝对精锐。

sentences.en: And on the 20th of August, so that's just to the day after I think Nelson has returned, he has a formal inspection in Boulogne.
sentences.zh: 在8月20日——我想这正好是纳尔逊归来后的一天——他在布洛涅进行了正式检阅。

sentences.en: And there is a plan.
sentences.zh: 并且有一个计划。

sentences.en: I mean, the plan has been made.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，计划已经制定好了。

sentences.en: That there would be a first wave of more than 100,000 men in 2,000 transports, and then a second wave of 50,000 men in another 600 transports.
sentences.zh: 第一波将由2000艘运输船运送超过10万名士兵，然后第二波由另外600艘运输船运送5万名士兵。

sentences.en: Now, we know that they don't come, and a lot of historians say it was actually never going to work, this plan.
sentences.zh: 现在我们知道他们没有来，许多历史学家说这个计划其实根本行不通。

sentences.en: But nobody knows this in Britain.
sentences.zh: 但在英国，没有人知道这一点。

sentences.en: And the newspapers in August 1805 are telling their readers, and I quote, the movements on the French coast have given rise to the belief
sentences.zh: 1805年8月的报纸在向读者宣告——我引用原话——法国海岸的动向让人相信

sentences.en: that the invasion of England will be attempted immediately.
sentences.zh: 对英格兰的入侵将随时付诸实施。

sentences.en: So there are all kinds of plans that have been made, a series of what are called optical
sentences.zh: 因此人们制定了各种计划，建立了一系列所谓的

sentences.en: telegraphs to link the Admiralty with Chatham, Tom, with Sheerness, with all these.
sentences.zh: 光学电报，将海军部与查塔姆、希尔内斯（Sheerness）以及所有这些地方连接起来，汤姆。

sentences.en: So these are people waving flags and stuff to communicate with each other on hills.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人是在山头挥舞旗帜之类来互相通信。

sentences.en: There are beacons.
sentences.zh: 有烽火台。

sentences.en: There are coastal batteries.
sentences.zh: 有海岸炮台。

sentences.en: They are working on the Martello Towers, which actually don't get finished until after the Battle of Trafalgar.
sentences.zh: 他们正在修建马特洛塔（Martello Towers），这些塔实际上直到特拉法加海战之后才完工。

sentences.en: And Dominic, what about the Sea Fensibles?
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，那海防民兵（Sea Fensibles）呢？

sentences.en: Well, the Sea Fensibles are the absolute crap troops, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 嗯，海防民兵绝对是一群废物部队，对吧？

sentences.en: People with one leg, disgruntled fishermen, anglers, whatever.
sentences.zh: 瘸一条腿的人、满腹牢骚的渔夫、垂钓者，诸如此类。

sentences.en: Touching heads.
sentences.zh: 碰头开会。

sentences.en: They've been called out.
sentences.zh: 他们被强召入伍了。

sentences.en: And actually, I have to say, almost 400,000 volunteers are drilling as Nelson arrives.
sentences.zh: 说实话，在纳尔逊抵达时，将近有40万志愿者在进行军事训练。

sentences.en: So people genuinely think this is going to happen.
sentences.zh: 所以人们真的认为这件事会发生。

sentences.en: There are contingency plans to close the stock exchange, to safeguard the gold reserves and the Bank of England, even to move the king and the government to the Midlands,
sentences.zh: 甚至还有应急计划，准备关闭证券交易所，保护黄金储备和英格兰银行，如果法国人真的成功登陆，甚至还要将国王和政府转移到中部地区。

sentences.en: should the French actually manage to land.
sentences.zh: 现在，小威廉·皮特（William Pitt）等人知道，控制海峡才是这一切的关键。

sentences.en: Now, William Pitt and co know that the control of the channel is what this is all about.
sentences.zh: 当然，这也是为什么维尔纳夫（Villeneuve）和格拉维纳（Gravina）组建联合舰队的消息会让伦敦陷入恐慌，因为联合舰队的人数将超过

sentences.en: And that's, of course, why London had been thrown into panic by the news of Villeneuve and Gravina forming the combined fleet, because the combined fleet would outnumber
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊的舰队。

sentences.en: Nelson's fleet.
sentences.zh: 而且他们也对这家伙怒不可遏，这家伙叫罗伯特·卡尔德（Robert Calder），他在维尔纳夫回家的路上拦截了他，

sentences.en: And they were also furious with this bloke, this bloke called Robert Calder, who had intercepted
sentences.zh: 基本上放跑了他让他逃到了费罗尔（Ferrol）。

sentences.en: Villeneuve on his way home and basically allowed him to escape to Ferrell.
sentences.zh: 所以每个人都在说，这个叫卡尔德的家伙毫无用处，这其实很不公平，因为联合舰队本该被彻底消灭的。

sentences.en: And so everyone is saying, oh, this guy Calder is useless, which is actually very unfair, because the combined fleet should have been killed off.
sentences.zh: 本来不应该让他们安全进入港口的。

sentences.en: It shouldn't have been allowed to get safe into port.
sentences.zh: 但这也提醒了人们一个绝对的假设，即进攻是皇家海军军官的天职，

sentences.en: But it is a reminder of the absolute assumption that it's the duty of a Royal Navy officer to attack,
sentences.zh: 正如伏尔泰所说，自打可怜的老海军上将拜恩（Admiral Byng）为了激励他人而在自己船的甲板上被枪决以来，情况一直如此。

sentences.en: which has been the case ever since poor old Admiral Bing got shot on the deck of his own boat to encourage the others, as Voltaire put it.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是全部的背景，解释了为什么纳尔逊回国会引起如此轰动的民众反响，为什么会有那种巨大而不断高涨的紧张感和兴奋感，

sentences.en: So this is all the context to explain why Nelson's return home is such a popular sensation, and why there is such a tremendous sense of mounting tension and excitement,
sentences.zh: 以及事件正加速走向决战的氛围。

sentences.en: of events speeding towards a showdown.
sentences.zh: 约翰·萨格登（John Sugden）在他那部精彩的纳尔逊传记中对此有一些极妙的评述。

sentences.en: John Sugden, in his brilliant biography of Nelson, has some excellent lines on this.
sentences.zh: 他说，那个夏天，无论纳尔逊走到哪里，都挥之不去一种感觉：自己正处于一场巨大且不断展开的戏剧中心，这场戏剧正不可阻挡地向着某个历史高潮凝聚加速。

sentences.en: He says, nowhere that summer could Nelson escape the feeling that he was in the center of a huge unfolding drama, inexorably gathering pace towards some historic climax.
sentences.zh: 他是国家的卫士，正武装自己以迎接决定性的较量。

sentences.en: He was the country's champion, arming himself for the decisive conteSt.
sentences.zh: 我们以前谈过这个，但我认为他真心觉得自己在这场冲突中是上帝的卫士，

sentences.en: And we talked about this before, but I think he genuinely feels that he is kind of God's champion in this,
sentences.zh: 这场正在酝酿的整场戏剧带有某种末日般的色彩。

sentences.en: that there is a kind of apocalyptic tinge to the whole drama that is brewing.
sentences.zh: 我也这么认为。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想他心里在想，听着，就是现在了。

sentences.en: I think he thinks, listen, this is it now.
sentences.zh: 如果我能消灭联合舰队，那就大功告成了。

sentences.en: If I can destroy the combined fleet, that is it.
sentences.zh: 海上战争就此结束。

sentences.en: The war at sea is over.
sentences.zh: 大局已定。

sentences.en: It is done.
sentences.zh: 英国是海洋的女王。

sentences.en: Britain is the mistress of the seas.
sentences.zh: 故事到此为止。

sentences.en: End of story.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在这种情况下，皇家海军可以接管法国和西班牙的贸易。

sentences.en: And actually, in that case, the Royal Navy can take over the French and Spanish trade.
sentences.zh: 它可以封锁他们的港口。

sentences.en: It can blockade their ports.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，我们可以把拿破仑挤压到投降。

sentences.en: And over time, we can squeeze Napoleon into surrender.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这就是后来的结果。

sentences.en: And basically, that is what happens.
sentences.zh: 这就是发生的事情。

sentences.en: That is what happens.
sentences.zh: 还有那种彻底歼灭的信条。

sentences.en: And that doctrine of annihilation.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们在这个系列里也一直在讨论这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, again, we've talked about this throughout the series.
sentences.zh: 这是纳尔逊绝对坚守的信条。

sentences.en: It's one that Nelson absolutely upholds.
sentences.zh: 但它本质上也是皇家海军的教条。

sentences.en: But it is also essentially Royal Navy dogma.
sentences.zh: 而且越来越成为一种正统观念：近身接敌，把敌舰炸沉在水里。

sentences.en: And increasingly, getting up close, blasting the enemy ships out of the water, this is becoming the orthodoxy.
sentences.zh: 但需要纳尔逊来将其奉为圭臬，并展现出它所能产生的全部毁灭性威力。

sentences.en: But it takes Nelson to enshrine it and to reveal the full devastating impact that it can have.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是的。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think that's right.
sentences.zh: 我认为这段时间里，他一直在脑海中反复琢磨这个计划，思考他要做什么。

sentences.en: I think all this time, he's turning over the plan in his mind, what he'll do.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他知道决战何时会到来。

sentences.en: You know, he knows when the showdown will come.
sentences.zh: 他在想，我将如何做到这一点？

sentences.en: And he's thinking, how will I do this?
sentences.zh: 有一个非常非常著名的故事。

sentences.en: There's a very, very famous story.
sentences.zh: 一个叫理查德·基茨（Richard Keats）的舰长拜访了默顿。

sentences.en: A guy called Captain Richard Keats visited Merton.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊和他散步时说，好吧，计划是这样的。

sentences.en: And Nelson went for a walk with him and said, okay, here is the plan.
sentences.zh: 当我看到联合舰队时，我会直接冲向他们。

sentences.en: I will go straight at the Combined Fleet when I see them.
sentences.zh: 我会有两个进攻纵队来冲散他们的战线。

sentences.en: I'll have two attacking columns to splinter their line.
sentences.zh: 他说，你觉得怎么样？

sentences.en: He says, what do you think of it?
sentences.zh: 我来告诉你我的看法。

sentences.en: I'll tell you what I think of it.
sentences.zh: 我认为这会让敌人大吃一惊并陷入混乱。

sentences.en: I think it will surprise and confound the enemy.
sentences.zh: 我想这会使敌人感到惊讶和困惑。

sentences.en: They won't know what I'm about.
sentences.zh: 他们不会知道我的意图。

sentences.en: It will bring forward a pell-mell battle.
sentences.zh: 这将引发一场混战。

sentences.en: And that's what I want.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我想要的。

sentences.en: So get in really close and go for it.
sentences.zh: 所以要贴得极近，全力出击。

sentences.en: So Adam Nicholson, in his brilliant book on Trafalgar, describes it as the introduction of chaos as a tool of battle.
sentences.zh: 因此，亚当·尼科尔森在他那本关于特拉法加海战的精彩著作中，将其描述为将混乱引入作为一种战斗工具。

sentences.en: Because the kind of the traditional naval battle is like a kind of a waltz, a minuet, like the kind of thing that you see in a Jane Austen adaptation.
sentences.zh: 因为那种传统的近代海战就像是一种华尔兹，一种小步舞曲，就像你在简·奥斯汀改编作品中看到的那种。

sentences.en: His plan is to totally upend that.
sentences.zh: 他的计划是彻底颠覆这一点。

sentences.en: And in the conditions of chaos, rely on the fact that British gunnery is so superior that the Royal Navy ships will inevitably emerge triumphant.
sentences.zh: 并在混乱的条件下，依靠英国炮术极其精湛这一事实，使皇家海军的舰艇最终必然取得胜利。

sentences.en: But will he get the chance?
sentences.zh: 但他能得到这个机会吗？

sentences.en: This is the question.
sentences.zh: 这就是问题所在。

sentences.en: So all the time, he's waiting and waiting and waiting for news.
sentences.zh: 因此，他一直在等待、等待、等待着消息。

sentences.en: And then at five o'clock in the morning, on Monday, the 2nd of September, a coach and four comes rattling down the drive towards Merton Place.
sentences.zh: 然后，在9月2日星期一清晨五点，一辆四马马车朝着默顿庄园疾驰而来。

sentences.en: And out gets this naval officer.
sentences.zh: 接着，这位海军军官下了车。

sentences.en: He's quite a stocky bloke.
sentences.zh: 他是个相当壮实的家伙。

sentences.en: He's come all the way by sea and by land.
sentences.zh: 他一路从水路和陆路赶来。

sentences.en: So he's covered with seawater and mud.
sentences.zh: 所以他身上沾满了海水和泥土。

sentences.en: And this guy is called Henry Blackwood.
sentences.zh: 这个人名叫亨利·布莱克伍德。

sentences.en: And he is the captain of the frigate Uriolus.
sentences.zh: 他是“尤里乌鲁斯”号护卫舰的舰长。

sentences.en: And he has come all the way from Cadiz with news from Admiral Collingwood, Cuthbert Collingwood, who's been keeping tabs on the Spanish port on the Spanish coaSt.
sentences.zh: 他一路从加的斯赶来，带来了海军上将科林伍德（卡瑟伯特·科林伍德）的消息，后者一直在监视西班牙海岸的那个西班牙港口。

sentences.en: And this is what Blackwood says to Nelson.
sentences.zh: 这就是布莱克伍德对纳尔逊说的话。

sentences.en: He says, Villeneuve has left Feral.
sentences.zh: 他说，维尔讷已经离开费罗尔。

sentences.en: He left two weeks ago on the 13th of AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 他在两周前的8月13日离开了。

sentences.en: He clearly was planning to head towards France, but he was deterred by the sight of British cruises.
sentences.zh: 他显然计划前往法国，但被英国巡洋舰的出现吓退了。

sentences.en: And he's turned around and gone south.
sentences.zh: 于是他掉头向南驶去。

sentences.en: Villeneuve has now taken refuge in the port at Cadiz.
sentences.zh: 维尔讷现在已经在加的斯的港口避难。

sentences.en: He and Gravina have almost 40 ships between them, but they're very short on morale and they're very short on food and water and supplies generally.
sentences.zh: 他和格拉维纳手下加起来有近40艘战舰，但他们的士气非常低落，而且极度缺乏食物、水和普遍的补给。

sentences.en: Now, in truth, Villeneuve is pretty much a kind of is a very demoralized, broken man.
sentences.zh: 说实话，维尔讷基本上是一个士气极其低落、心力交瘁的人。

sentences.en: Villeneuve has lost faith completely in his emperor's plan, which he always thought was mad.
sentences.zh: 维尔讷已经彻底对皇帝的计划失去了信心，他一直认为这个计划是疯狂的。

sentences.en: To be fair, the emperor has also lost faith in him, which is also preying on Villeneuve's mind.
sentences.zh: 平心而论，皇帝对他也失去了信心，这也一直萦绕在维尔讷的心头。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Now, Nelson doesn't know this, but he does know that Villeneuve cannot stay in Cadiz for long because there will not be enough supplies.
sentences.zh: 现在，纳尔逊并不知道这一点，但他知道维尔讷在加的斯呆不久，因为补给会不够。

sentences.en: He will have to leave to find supplies.
sentences.zh: 他将不得不离开去寻找补给。

sentences.en: And when he does, you know, this is it.
sentences.zh: 而当他这样做时，你知道的，机会就来了。

sentences.en: But Dominic also, there's the risk, isn't there, that he might go into the Mediterranean, which would cause chaos, or he might head northwards.
sentences.zh: 但多米尼克，这也存在风险，不是吗？他可能会进入地中海，那将引发混乱，或者他可能会向北驶去。

sentences.en: So there's opportunity, but there is also risk in Villeneuve and the Spanish breaking out.
sentences.zh: 因此，维尔讷和西班牙人突围既有机遇，也存在风险。

sentences.en: Because there's another Spanish fleet at Cartagena.
sentences.zh: 因为在卡塔赫纳还有另一支西班牙舰队。

sentences.en: And if Villeneuve was to link up with them and then to head into the Mediterranean, who knows where he could go?
sentences.zh: 如果维尔讷与他们会合，然后驶入地中海，谁知道他会去哪里呢？

sentences.en: So Sardinia, Sicily, Naples, Egypt again, you know, or what if he then makes for the Channel?
sentences.zh: 所以可能是萨丁尼亚、西西里、那不勒斯、埃及，或者如果他接着驶向英吉利海峡呢？

sentences.en: So Nelson thinks, right, this is my chance.
sentences.zh: 因此纳尔逊心想，好，这就是我的机会。

sentences.en: The stakes are very high.
sentences.zh: 赌注非常高。

sentences.en: If I can annihilate Villeneuve now, then the war is won at sea.
sentences.zh: 如果我现在能消灭维尔讷，那么海战就赢了。

sentences.en: So within hours, he's jumped into a carriage and he is heading into London.
sentences.zh: 所以在几小时内，他跳上一辆马车，正朝伦敦驶去。

sentences.en: He goes straight to the Admiralty.
sentences.zh: 他径直前往海军部。

sentences.en: Then he goes to Downing Street to meet William Pitt and the First Lord, Lord Barham.
sentences.zh: 然后他去唐宁街会见威廉·皮特和第一海军大臣巴勒姆勋爵。

sentences.en: Nelson says, you know, give me the chance.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊说，你知道的，给我这个机会。

sentences.en: I want to strike immediately.
sentences.zh: 我想要立即发起进攻。

sentences.en: That will eliminate the threat of invasion.
sentences.zh: 这将消除入侵的威胁。

sentences.en: That will give us command of the Mediterranean forever.
sentences.zh: 这将使我们永远获得对地中海的控制权。

sentences.en: And as he later told a friend of his, George Rose, who was a confidant of William Pitt, he said, it is annihilation that the country wants, not merely a splendid victory.
sentences.zh: 正如他后来对他的朋友乔治·罗斯（威廉·皮特的知己）所说的那样，国家想要的不是一次辉煌的胜利，而是彻底的消灭。

sentences.en: So this is going to be a different kind of battle.
sentences.zh: 所以这将是一场不同寻常的战斗。

sentences.en: The question is, will he get enough ships?
sentences.zh: 问题是，他能得到足够多的战舰吗？

sentences.en: Lord Barham says, look, I've only got about 70 ships of the line fit for service to cover the entire globe.
sentences.zh: 巴勒姆勋爵说，听着，我手里只有大约70艘适合服役的列阵战舰来应对全球各地的局势。

sentences.en: But he says, I will back you.
sentences.zh: 但他接着说，我会支持你的。

sentences.en: Go back to Cadiz, take over the victory and take command of the fleet.
sentences.zh: 回到加的斯，接管“胜利”号并指挥舰队。

sentences.en: You can name your own officers.
sentences.zh: 你可以亲自指定军官。

sentences.en: I will send you whatever ships I can.
sentences.zh: 我会尽可能多地派给你战舰。

sentences.en: You're probably going to get about 27 in total.
sentences.zh: 你总共大概能得到27艘左右。

sentences.en: And let us hope that is enough.
sentences.zh: 但愿这足够了。

sentences.en: And your instructions, I'll leave it very simple.
sentences.zh: 至于你的指令，我就说得非常简单。

sentences.en: To protect Britain's trade, to prevent the enemy getting to sea, everything else is up to you.
sentences.zh: 保护英国的贸易，阻止敌人出海，其他一切都由你做主。

sentences.en: You handle it as you see fit.
sentences.zh: 你认为怎么合适就怎么处理。

sentences.en: And I think, don't you, that this is the Admiralty and the Prime Minister and the government buying into this sense of Nelson's destiny, that fate has brought him to this point.
sentences.zh: 我想，海军部、首相和政府其实也是在顺应纳尔逊的命运感，觉得是命运把他带到了这一刻，不是吗？

sentences.en: And they are kind of going, yes, go for it.
sentences.zh: 他们可以说是赞同说，去干吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是的。

sentences.en: You can really sense the mood at this point.
sentences.zh: 你真的能感觉到当时的这种情绪。

sentences.en: This sort of sense that John Sutton described of events hastening towards an inevitable conclusion.
sentences.zh: 约翰·萨顿所描述的那种事件正加速走向不可避免的结局的感觉。

sentences.en: And they were all really buying into this.
sentences.zh: 他们都非常认同这一点。

sentences.en: The very next day, it started to rain.
sentences.zh: 就在第二天，天开始下雨了。

sentences.en: And, you know, this sort of fantastic example of the kind of pathetic fallacy.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这是一个绝佳的情感谬误的例子。

sentences.en: It starts to rain, grey skies.
sentences.zh: 天开始下雨，天空灰蒙蒙的。

sentences.en: Emma Hamilton has been very downcast by the news that Villeneuve is out.
sentences.zh: 埃玛·汉密尔顿听到维尔讷出海的消息后感到非常沮丧。

sentences.en: She had hoped that Nelson would be ashore for months.
sentences.zh: 她原本希望纳尔逊能在岸上待上几个月。

sentences.en: But once again, the clock is ticking.
sentences.zh: 但时光再次流逝。

sentences.en: And she writes this letter, doesn't she, to Lady Kitty Bolton.
sentences.zh: 她写了这封信，不是吗，写给基蒂·博尔顿爵士夫人。

sentences.en: It seems as though I've had a fortnight's dream and I'm awoke to all the misery of this cruel separation.
sentences.zh: 这似乎就像我做了一场长达两周的梦，醒来后面对的却是这场残酷离别带来的所有痛苦。

sentences.en: But what can I do?
sentences.zh: 但我能怎么办呢？

sentences.en: His powerful arm is of so much consequence to his country.
sentences.zh: 他强有力的臂膀对他的国家有着如此重大的影响。

sentences.en: But I cannot say more.
sentences.zh: 但我不能再多说了。

sentences.en: My heart is broken.
sentences.zh: 我的心碎了。

sentences.en: Of course, Nelson doesn't have that much time to think about this because he's thinking about his plan.
sentences.zh: 当然，纳尔逊没有那么多时间去想这些，因为他在考虑自己的计划。

sentences.en: He is anxious whether he's going to have enough ships.
sentences.zh: 他一直在担心自己是否有足够的战舰。

sentences.en: He's thinking about this business, about smashing them into fragments.
sentences.zh: 他在琢磨这件事，也就是把他们炸得粉碎。

sentences.en: So he's rushing back and forth across London, making all the preparations, getting all the stuff ready, making sure they'll have enough supplies.
sentences.zh: 所以他在伦敦奔波忙碌，做着各种准备工作，备齐所有的物资，确保他们有足够的补给。

sentences.en: You know, is he going to link up the victory, all of this kind of thing?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他要去和“胜利”号会合吗，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: Interestingly, there is a sense of fatalism, I think, to Nelson, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，纳尔逊身上有一种宿命论的感觉，对吧？

sentences.en: There's a sense that he knows this could be it for him.
sentences.zh: 有一种感觉，他知道这可能就是他的人生终点。

sentences.en: And I think that that's not just fatalism.
sentences.zh: 我认为这不仅仅是宿命论。

sentences.en: I think that's realism.
sentences.zh: 我认为那是现实主义。

sentences.en: Because as we've been saying, his plan is to form two columns that will drive straight into the French and Spanish lines,
sentences.zh: 因为正如我们一直在说的，他的计划是组成两列纵队，直接冲入法军和西军的阵线，

sentences.en: which is ripping up the orthodoxy of how you fight a battle.
sentences.zh: 这完全打破了传统作战的正统观念。

sentences.en: And I'm sure by this point, there's no question that he, on victory, is going to be leading one of those two columns.
sentences.zh: 而且我确信到了这个时候，毫无疑问他将在“胜利”号上率领其中一列纵队。

sentences.en: And that means that he will be directly in the line of fire because essentially he can't ask his men to risk such a dangerous course of action and not himself be in the forefront of the fighting.
sentences.zh: 这意味着他将直接处于火线之中，因为本质上他不能要求他的手下去冒如此危险的险，而自己却不冲在战斗的最前沿。

sentences.en: So he must think, you know, I'm going to be in more danger in this battle than I've ever been before.
sentences.zh: 所以他一定在想，你知道的，在这场战斗中我将面临比以往任何时候都更大的危险。

sentences.en: And doubtless, he has told Emma this.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问，他已经把这一点告诉了埃玛。

sentences.en: And that's why she is, well, lacrimose would be an unfair word.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么她——好吧，用“泪流满面”来形容可能不太贴切。

sentences.en: I mean, that's why she's so devastated at the thought of him leaving.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是为什么一想到他要离开，她就如此痛不欲生。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是的。

sentences.en: So his last full day is Thursday, the 12th of September.
sentences.zh: 所以他的最后一个完整的一天是9月12日星期四。

sentences.en: And again, he spends most of it in London.
sentences.zh: 同样，他大部分时间都在伦敦度过。

sentences.en: He goes to see Lord Castle Ray at the Colonial Office in Downing Street.
sentences.zh: 他去唐宁街的殖民地办公室拜访了卡尔斯雷勋爵。

sentences.en: Very famous incident.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常著名的事件。

sentences.en: And Nelson is shown into an anteroom to wait for Lord Castle Ray.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊被领进一间前厅等待卡尔斯雷勋爵。

sentences.en: And another man is waiting there who's a short man, another short man, who has a very distinctive kind of beaky nose.
sentences.zh: 里面还另有一个人在等待，个子很矮，又是个矮个子，有着非常独特的鹰钩鼻。

sentences.en: And this other man makes some sort of polite small talk to Nelson.
sentences.zh: 这个陌生人跟纳尔逊寒暄了几句。

sentences.en: But Nelson is tired and, of course, he's nervous and he's excited and distracted.
sentences.zh: 但纳尔逊很累，而且当然，他很紧张、兴奋又有些分心。

sentences.en: And the other man said afterwards, he could not know who I was, but he entered at once into conversation with me, if I can call it conversation.
sentences.zh: 那个人后来回忆说，他可能不知道我是谁，但他立刻跟我攀谈起来，如果这能算作谈话的话。

sentences.en: For it was almost all on his side and all about himself and in really a style so vain and so silly as to surprise and almost disgust me.
sentences.zh: 因为几乎全都是他在说，而且全都是关于他自己，那种自负和愚蠢的做派实在让人惊讶，甚至让我感到有些反感。

sentences.en: So that's the tone of Lord Minto visiting Merton and seeing all the Nelson memorabilia everywhere.
sentences.zh: 这就是访默顿、看到到处都是纳尔逊纪念品的明托勋爵的语气。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So Nelson just talking about himself.
sentences.zh: 所以纳尔逊只是在谈论他自己。

sentences.en: Then the other man must have said something that made Nelson think because Nelson then went out and he had a word with the clerk or the official outside, obviously,
sentences.zh: 然后那个人一定说了什么话，让纳尔逊陷入了沉思，因为纳尔逊随后走了出去，显然跟外面的办事员或官员交谈了一番，

sentences.en: to find out who this bloke was.
sentences.zh: 去查明这家伙是谁。

sentences.en: And then he came in and was completely transformed because this man is Major General Sir Arthur Wellesley, who is just back from India,
sentences.zh: 接着他走进来，整个人完全变了，因为这个人是阿瑟·韦尔斯利少将，他刚刚从印度归来，

sentences.en: having been smiting the Maharata Empire and keeping India for the East India Company.
sentences.zh: 此前他一直在打击马拉塔帝国并为东印度公司守护印度。

sentences.en: And he is, of course, the future Duke of Wellington and Wellington said, when Nelson came back in, he was altogether a different man, both in manner and matter.
sentences.zh: 他当然就是未来的威灵顿公爵，威灵顿说，当纳尔逊再次走进来时，他无论是在举止还是谈吐上都完全变成了另一个人。

sentences.en: What Wellington called his charlatan style had vanished.
sentences.zh: 威灵顿所说的他那种江湖郎中的做派已经消失了。

sentences.en: And he talked about strategy and politics with a good sense and a knowledge that surprised me equally and more agreeably than the first part of our interview had done.
sentences.zh: 他谈论战略和政治时的见解和知识，给我的惊讶和愉悦甚至超过了我们初次见面时。

sentences.en: And he talked like an officer and a statesman.
sentences.zh: 他的谈吐像一名军官和政治家。

sentences.en: I don't know that I've ever had a conversation that interested me more.
sentences.zh: 我不记得自己曾有过哪次谈话比这更让我感兴趣。

sentences.en: There you have the two.
sentences.zh: 这就是两人的对比。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, this is after the event, so maybe there's a tiny pinch of salt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然这是事后回忆的，所以可能要打一点折扣。

sentences.en: It plays very well for Wellington, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 这对威灵顿来说树立了很好的形象，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because on the one hand, it makes him look good, but it also subtly makes Nelson look a bit of a coxcomb.
sentences.zh: 因为一方面，这让他显得很好，但另一方面也微妙地让纳尔逊显得有点像个自负的家伙。

sentences.en: But that said, this is Nelson to a T, right?
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，这确实是典型的纳尔逊风格，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, Nelson would have just talked about himself and being completely vain and self-interested.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，纳尔逊当时肯定一直在谈论自己，表现得完全虚荣且利己。

sentences.en: Well, maybe.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许吧。

sentences.en: I think Nelson has a capacity to take an interest in someone else.
sentences.zh: 我认为纳尔逊有能力去对别人产生兴趣。

sentences.en: He has lapses.
sentences.zh: 他也有状态不佳的时候。

sentences.en: I mean, he's often had lapses.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他经常有失水准的时候。

sentences.en: Remember that time when he was going from Naples all the way through Vienna and Prague and whatnot, and he wasn't always showing himself to his best side then.
sentences.zh: 还记得他从那不勒斯一路经由维也纳、布拉格等地的那次经历吗，他当时并非总能展现出自己最好的一面。

sentences.en: Anyway, he's had that meeting with Lord Carcerin.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，他和卡尔斯雷勋爵的会面结束了。

sentences.en: His very last meeting is at Number 10 Downing Street, and this is his farewell to William Pitt.
sentences.zh: 他的最后一次会面是在唐宁街10号，这是他向威廉·皮特的告别。

sentences.en: We don't know what was said, but we do know that Pitt unusually is said to have come down with Nelson and escorted him to his carriage,
sentences.zh: 我们不知道他们谈了什么，但我们确实知道，据说皮特很不寻常地亲自下楼陪同纳尔逊并把他送上了马车，

sentences.en: which was a marked gesture, I think, of affection and respect, because Pitt didn't usually do this.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个明显的充满温情和敬意的举动，因为皮特通常不会这么做。

sentences.en: Actually, on his way out of town, there is one last thing.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在离开镇子的时候，还有最后一件事。

sentences.en: He makes sure, he stops to make sure that the very latest signal book has been sent to the fleet.
sentences.zh: 他确保、他特意停下来确保将最新版本的信号手册发送给舰队。

sentences.en: A good example, actually, of attention to detail.
sentences.zh: 这其实是一个注重细节的好例子。

sentences.en: Nelson knows these little things could really make a difference.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊知道这些小事真的能发挥巨大的作用。

sentences.en: Do you think he already has a zingy slogan in mind?
sentences.zh: 你觉得他脑子里已经想好了一条振奋人心的标语了吗？

sentences.en: Well, a slogan that actually, as we'll find out, has to be corrected by his signals, Lieutenant, because he's trying to send a message for which there's no code.
sentences.zh: 嗯，正如我们后面会发现的那样，这条标语实际上必须由他的信号中尉来纠正，因为他试图发送一条没有对应密码的信息。

sentences.en: Anyway, we're jumping ahead.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样，我们言归正传。

sentences.en: Back he goes to Merton.
sentences.zh: 他回到了默顿。

sentences.en: He's there in time for dinner.
sentences.zh: 他在晚饭前赶到了那里。

sentences.en: But it's a pretty sad occasion.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个相当令人伤感的场合。

sentences.en: Lord Minto, who is there, said that Emma could not eat and hardly drink and was near swooning.
sentences.zh: 在场的明托勋爵说，埃玛难过得吃不下饭，几乎喝不下水，甚至快要晕厥过去。

sentences.en: And Lord Minto, who's no Emma fan, found all this very over the top and very sort of showy and performative.
sentences.zh: 而并不怎么喜欢埃玛的明托勋爵，觉得这一切都太夸张了，显得很做作、很爱演。

sentences.en: So Emma is clearly very, very upset.
sentences.zh: 所以埃玛显然非常非常难过。

sentences.en: You know, Nelson is going away and maybe this will be for the last time.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，纳尔逊要走了，也许这会是最后一次。

sentences.en: He will have shared the odds with her.
sentences.zh: 他曾与她风雨同舟。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, I don't think he's performative at all.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道的，我觉得他一点也不做作。

sentences.en: I think if you're in love with someone and he's going off and likely to die, I think you're allowed the occasional tear.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你爱上一个人，而他即将离去且很可能会死，偶尔流泪是被允许的。

sentences.en: Oh, you're soft-hearted.
sentences.zh: 哦，你真是心软。

sentences.en: So the next day is Friday, the 13th of September.
sentences.zh: 所以第二天是9月13日，星期五。

sentences.en: It's the last day of their lives together.
sentences.zh: 这是他们共度人生的最后一天。

sentences.en: It's a cloudy, windy day, and they are stuck inside in Merton.
sentences.zh: 那天多云且有风，他们被困在默顿的室内。

sentences.en: Now, it may be today that there's a sort of celebrated incident.
sentences.zh: 现在，今天可能会发生某种著名的事件。

sentences.en: They took communion together, Nelson and Emma, and they exchanged gold rings in what they called a private sacrament.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊和爱玛一起领了圣餐，并在他们所谓的私人圣礼中交换了金戒指。

sentences.en: So biographers often describe this as kind of unofficial betrothal or marriage ceremony.
sentences.zh: 因此传记作家经常将此描述为一种非官方的订婚或结婚仪式。

sentences.en: Nelson, of course, is married already to Fanny.
sentences.zh: 当然，纳尔逊已经娶了范妮。

sentences.en: His ring, which I think recently came up for auction, it was mounted with a large H and was actually engraved with the date, the 13th of September, probably afterward.
sentences.zh: 他的戒指——我想最近才被拿出来拍卖过——上面镶嵌着一个大写字母H，并且可能是在事后被刻上了9月13日的日期。

sentences.en: Well, it must have been afterwards, I guess, which suggests that they did something because they know, as you've said, this could be it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我猜一定是在事后，这表明他们确实做了一些事，因为他们知道，正如你所说，这可能是最后一次。

sentences.en: This could be the last time they ever see each other.
sentences.zh: 这可能是他们最后一次相见。

sentences.en: You know, it's a very humdrum day.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这是极其平凡的一天。

sentences.en: Nelson's doing a lot of chores.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊在做很多琐事。

sentences.en: He's making a lot of arrangements to pay, you know, bills.
sentences.zh: 他在做许多安排来支付账单。

sentences.en: Bills for prints, no doubt of himself, and wine and whatnot, and architects' bills.
sentences.zh: 毫无疑问有他自己肖像版画的账单，还有酒水之类的，以及建筑师的账单。

sentences.en: The coach has been ordered for 10 o'clock that evening to take him down to the coast to the victory.
sentences.zh: 马车已经订好于当晚10点来接他去海岸的“胜利号”上。

sentences.en: Night falls.
sentences.zh: 夜幕降临。

sentences.en: The hour approaches.
sentences.zh: 时间逼近。

sentences.en: The scene that you described earlier, he goes up to Horatia to say goodbye.
sentences.zh: 你刚才描述的那个场景，他走过去向霍拉蒂娅道别。

sentences.en: The coach is loaded.
sentences.zh: 马车已经装好了行李。

sentences.en: Emma is in tears.
sentences.zh: 爱玛泪流满面。

sentences.en: She won't come outside.
sentences.zh: 她不肯出来。

sentences.en: Nelson comes back in four times from the coach, and finally he does this thing where he kneels and asks God his blessing, and he says these lines that, Tom, you find very moving.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊从马车那里折返回来四次，最后他做了那件事：他单膝跪地祈求上帝的保佑，并说出了那些——汤姆，你觉得非常感人的台词。

sentences.en: If there were more Emmas, there would be more Nelsons and all of this.
sentences.zh: 如果世上有更多的爱玛，就会有更多的纳尔逊，诸如此类。

sentences.en: But that's not the last exchange, actually.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，这并不是最后的对话。

sentences.en: The very last exchange is with his brother-in-law, George Matcham,
sentences.zh: 最后的对话是与他的小舅子乔治·马查姆进行的，

sentences.en: who's married to Nelson's sister.
sentences.zh: 他娶了纳尔逊的姐姐。

sentences.en: And Nelson says to George,
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊对乔治说，

sentences.en: I'm actually really sorry that I haven't done more for our family.
sentences.zh: 我其实真的很遗憾，我没有为我们的家族做更多的事情。

sentences.en: You know, I should have done more, made more money.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我本该做更多，赚更多钱的。

sentences.en: Maybe this time I'll get some prize money.
sentences.zh: 也许这次我会得到一些赏金。

sentences.en: And George says to him, we want for nothing.
sentences.zh: 乔治对他说，我们什么都不缺。

sentences.en: All that matters to us is that you're safe.
sentences.zh: 对我们来说，最重要的只有你平平安安。

sentences.en: And away Nelson goes into the night, and then he writes that moving journal entry that you read out, where he's, again, thinking about his own death.
sentences.zh: 随后纳尔逊消失在夜色中，接着他写下了你所朗读的那篇感人的日记，在日记中他再次想到了自己的死亡。

sentences.en: If it's God's good providence to cut short my days on earth, I bow with the greatest submission, and he hopes that God will protect those so dear to me that I leave behind.
sentences.zh: 如果承蒙上帝的眷顾缩短我在世的寿日，我必以最谦卑的姿态顺从，他希望上帝能保护那些我留下的、我深爱的人。

sentences.en: And as we'll see next time, that's a running theme, even in extremis, before the battle and after the battle,
sentences.zh: 正如我们下次将看到的，这是一个贯穿始终的主题，甚至在绝境中、在战斗前以及战斗后，

sentences.en: Nelson is thinking about those people that he's left behind.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊都一直在想着那些他留下的人。

sentences.en: At six o'clock the following morning, his carriage arrives at the George Inn at Portsmouth.
sentences.zh: 第二天早上六点，他的马车抵达了朴次茅斯的乔治客栈。

sentences.en: And Nelson writes a note to Emma.
sentences.zh: 纳尔逊给爱玛写了一张便条。

sentences.en: My dearest and most beloved of women,
sentences.zh: 我最亲爱、最深爱的女人，

sentences.en: Emma, Nelson's Emma, I arrived here.
sentences.zh: 爱玛，纳尔逊的爱玛，我到这里了。

sentences.en: Victory is at St. Helens.
sentences.zh: “胜利号”停在圣海伦斯。

sentences.en: If possible, I shall be away at sea this day.
sentences.zh: 如果可能的话，我今天就会出海。

sentences.en: God protect you, my dear Horatia.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑你，我亲爱的霍拉蒂娅。

sentences.en: Portsmouth is a port preparing for war.
sentences.zh: 朴次茅斯是一个正在为战争做准备的港口。

sentences.en: Carts and wagons everywhere, loads of people.
sentences.zh: 到处都是手推车和大车，挤满了人。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a great dockyard.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这是一个巨大的造船厂。

sentences.en: It's one of the great motors of Britain's war efforts.
sentences.zh: 它是英国战争机器的重要发动机之一。

sentences.en: And Nelson, actually, before he leaves, this is a lovely detail, he has the time to visit a new manufactory that is almost ready to kind of go online at Portsmouth,
sentences.zh: 而纳尔逊在离开之前——这是一个非常可爱的细节——他抽出时间去参观了一家即将完工并准备在朴次茅斯投入运营的新工厂，

sentences.en: which is this block mills powered by steam.
sentences.zh: 也就是这个由蒸汽驱动的滑轮厂。

sentences.en: It's the most advanced factory on earth.
sentences.zh: 这是地球上最先进的工厂。

sentences.en: It has been designed by a French exile called Marc Isambard Brunel.
sentences.zh: 它由一位名叫马克·伊桑巴德·布鲁奈尔的法国流亡者设计。
zh_words: 马克·伊桑巴德·布鲁奈尔

sentences.en: And it has machines basically to create these blocks, these kind of blocks.
sentences.zh: 它拥有专门制造这些滑轮、这种滑轮的机器。

sentences.en: I don't quite understand what these blocks do.
sentences.zh: 我不太明白这些滑轮是干什么用的。

sentences.en: They're kind of to do with pulleys, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 它们似乎跟滑轮组有关，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, pulleys and ropes.
sentences.zh: 是的，滑轮和绳索。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全正确。

sentences.en: So brilliant rope work.
sentences.zh: 所以是非常出色的绳索工程。

sentences.en: And the amazing detail that I remember from our previous series is that there was machinery operating in Portsmouth when Nelson left on Victory that was still operating in 1982
sentences.zh: 我从我们之前的系列节目中记得的一个惊人细节是，当纳尔逊乘坐“胜利号”离开时，朴次茅斯运转的机械直到1982年

sentences.en: when the Falklands Task Force left.
sentences.zh: 当福克兰群岛特遣舰队出发时仍在运转。

sentences.en: I mean, it's incredible.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: That's a crazy detail, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是一个疯狂的细节，不是吗？

sentences.en: So he goes back to the George Inn after that.
sentences.zh: 在那之后，他回到了乔治客栈。

sentences.en: He goes through a back door to avoid the crowds and he's going to leave from the beach by the bathing machines.
sentences.zh: 他从后门进去以避开人群，并打算从浴场旁的沙滩上乘船离开。

sentences.en: So a nice Emma-related touch there.
sentences.zh: 所以那里有一个很好的与爱玛相关的细节。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: It's not the normal place.
sentences.zh: 这不是通常的地点。

sentences.en: He's trying to escape the crowds, but actually there are hundreds of people waiting.
sentences.zh: 他试图避开人群，但实际上有成百上千的人在等待。

sentences.en: And as he comes down to the boarding point, there are people kneeling on the ground.
sentences.zh: 当他来到登船点时，有人跪在地上。

sentences.en: There are people cheering.
sentences.zh: 有人在欢呼。

sentences.en: There are people trying to touch his coat.
sentences.zh: 有人试图去摸他的外套。

sentences.en: Some people are in tears.
sentences.zh: 有些人泪流满面。

sentences.en: And as his boat pushes away towards the victory, they give him three cheers and he waves his hat in farewell.
sentences.zh: 当他的小船向“胜利号”划去时，他们向他发出三声欢呼，他挥舞着帽子告别。

sentences.en: And then very famously, Nelson murmurs, I had their huzzahs before.
sentences.zh: 然后，非常著名的是，纳尔逊喃喃自语道，我以前也听过他们的欢呼。

sentences.en: I have their hearts now.
sentences.zh: 但我现在得到了他们的心。

sentences.en: And by 11.30, he is on the victory and his last voyage begins.
sentences.zh: 到11点30分，他已经在“胜利号”上了，他最后的航程开始了。

sentences.en: Unbelievable drama.
sentences.zh: 难以置信的戏剧性。

sentences.en: My heart is beating so fast that I need to go and calm down.
sentences.zh: 我的心脏跳得太快了，我需要去冷静一下。

sentences.en: But we will be back in a few minutes to continue the story of Nelson's journey to Trafalgar.
sentences.zh: 但我们将在几分钟后回来，继续讲述纳尔逊驶向特拉法加的旅程。

sentences.zh: 本集由 Claude 的幕后团队 Anthropic 赞助播出。

sentences.zh: 历史上最迷人的问题往往没有简单的答案。

sentences.zh: 认识一下 Claude，专为深度思考而构建的人工智能。

sentences.en: The great game.
sentences.zh: 大博弈。

sentences.en: Strategic struggle between Britain and Russia.
sentences.zh: 英国与俄国之间的战略争端。

sentences.en: We assess our prime minister.
sentences.zh: 我们对我们的首相进行评估。

sentences.en: With high confidence it was Russian.
sentences.zh: 我们高度确信那是俄罗斯干的。

sentences.en: Holding the Russians accountable is World War III.
sentences.zh: 让俄罗斯人承担责任就等于第三次世界大战。

sentences.en: They took down a British passenger jet containing 350 people.
sentences.zh: 他们击落了一架载有350人的英国客机。

sentences.en: Man in the Kremlin is playing, Alex.
sentences.zh: 克里姆林宫的那个人在玩火，亚历克斯。

sentences.en: You've got to ask yourself, you want to play or not?
sentences.zh: 你得问问自己，你想不想陪他玩？

sentences.en: You're the prime minister.
sentences.zh: 你可是首相。

sentences.en: You've done nothing!
sentences.zh: 你什么都没做！

sentences.en: We would need to understand the policy context.
sentences.zh: 我们需要了解政策背景。
